chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Aqeeqa, is it obligatory? He said: Yes, it is obligatory.

key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةِ: Aqeeqa, the ritual sacrifice offered for a newborn child
key_terms.وَاجِبَةٌ: Obligatory/Mandatory (a specific level of legal duty in Shia fiqh)

ai.seo_question: Is Aqeeqa obligatory in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This concise narration from al-Kafi establishes the obligatory status (wajib) of Aqeeqa, distinguishing it from the more debated sunnah status in other schools. It reflects the Imami juristic view that the sacrifice for a newborn is a binding religious duty, underscoring the gratitude owed to Allah for the blessing of progeny. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan narrators, such as Abu Basir, in preserving these legal rulings from Imam al-Sadiq.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about the Aqeeqa, is it Obligatory?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, Obligatory’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from abu Basir who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about ‘ Aqiqah : if it is obligatory or not.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is obligatory.’”
